items.title: CAT Jammu imposes ₹10,000 cost on Senior Advocate for appearing without uniform
items.summary: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)'s Jammu Bench has imposed costs of ₹10,000 on Senior Advocate Jahangir Ganai for appearing without uniform during virtual proceedings and making derogatory remarks "about the Court". A Bench of Judicial Member Diwakar Singh and Administrative Member Ram Mohan Johri directed that the cost be deposited within a period of one week. "He seems to be unapologetic for his appearance without uniform," the bench recorded in the order passed on October 7. According to the order, Ganai initially appeared through audio mode and began making submissions without switching on his video. After repeated requests, he switched on the video, revealing he was not in uniform. "While the matter was under discussion, he made derogatory remarks upon the Court," it noted. Ganai was representing a respondent in a service matter. Senior Advocate Abhinav Sharma assisted by advocate Vishal Sharma appeared for the applicant. Additional Advocate General Rajesh Thappa appeared for the State. Senior Advocate Pawan Kundal with advocate Jagdeep Kour and Senior Advocate Jahangir Ganai also appeared for the respondents. [Read Order]

items.title: Our forgiving nature must end: Supreme Court on leniency to death row convicts
items.summary: In a stark moment of judicial self-reflection, the Supreme Court on Thursday criticised its habit of showing leniency to murder convicts, particularly those facing the death penalty. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu remarked that the Court's "forgiving nature" has at times backfired and caused problems. Justice Datta opined that the court needs to re-evaluate its traditional restraint when examining whether the death penalty should be awarded in murder cases. "Times have changed. In earlier days murder leading to death (sentence) was on the basis of rarest of rare cases, because murders were rare. Is it the same now? Now murder is not a rare (offence)," Justice Datta observed. The judge recounted a past case where the Supreme Court commuted the death sentence of a convict, only for him to commit another horrific crime after being released on parole. "It is because of our forgiving nature that India is facing these problems. Forgive, forgive, forgive, you have to draw a line somewhere. items.title: Karnataka High Court stays proceedings against Minister Laxman Savadi in 2018 assault case

Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde passed the interim order after observing that the procedure followed by the Athani trial court in summoning Savadi appeared to be contrary to law. “I am not on the merits; I am on the procedure. There cannot be chief examination thereafter?” the Court observed. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The case relates to an incident during a foundation-laying ceremony attended by Savadi in 2018, who was then an MLA. According to the prosecution case, the complainant had questioned Savadi, following which the latter's driver, personal assistant and supporters allegedly assaulted him. items.title: Shishtachar squads, beat patrolling, cab driver checks: Supreme Court issues directives for women's safety in Delhi
items.summary: The Supreme Court has issued a series of binding directions to revamp preventive policing, public transport security, and monitoring across the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to ensure the safety of women [ In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR ]. The directions form part of the ongoing suo motu proceedings initiated by the Court after a spate of rape cases were reported recently from Delhi-NCR, including a case where a teenager was raped at a public park. In its order, the Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran emphasised that public safety requires continuous ground visibility rather than post-incident response. The Court observed that unmonitored dark stretches, broken streetlights, and illegal eateries directly facilitate crimes against women. "Public safety... cannot be viewed solely through the prism of a response to a crime after it has occurred. The manner in which public spaces are maintained, the visibility of police patrolling and surveillance, and the promptness with which reported deficiencies are addressed are equally relevant to crime prevention," the Court noted in its October 5 order. items.title: Women can't be booked for offence of sex on false promise to marry: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that a woman cannot be accused of the offence of having sexual intercourse through deceitful means or a false promise to marry under Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde held the same while partially quashing criminal proceedings under Section 69, BNS, 2023 against a woman. "Admittedly, the petitioner is a women and is arrayed as accused No.2 and the offence under Section 69 of the BNS, 2023, cannot be attracted against the petitioner and the allegations in the complaint do not indicate any such act by the petitioner." Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The complainant in the case was a woman who claimed that she had sexual relations with the petitioner's husband. The husband allegedly promised to marry the complainant after saying that his relationship with his wife was not cordial. The complainant also alleged that the husband and wife had taken photos and videos of her, shared them with third parties without her consent and attempted to blackmail her. items.title: Refusing to marry live-in partner does not by itself amount to abetment of suicide: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that refusing to marry a live-in partner, followed by the partner’s suicide, does not by itself amount to the offence of abetment of suicide without intentional instigation or knowledge that such refusal would have led to suicide. A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran made the observation while quashing criminal proceedings against six accused, including the woman's partner, his parents, sister and others. The Court observed that the allegations, even if accepted as stated by the complainant, did not establish any act of instigation by the accused to drive the woman to suicide. “People react differently to situations and if a breakup ends up with suicide, it cannot always be termed an abetment to suicide. The refusal to marry was not with an intention to drive the woman to death by suicide nor can knowledge be attributed to the accused that on such refusal, she would commit suicide,” said the Court. items.title: Lord Buddha on saree pallu: Gujarat High Court quashes case accusing trader of hurting religious feelings

Justice PM Raval ruled that one cannot automatically presume that selling textile materials containing artistic depictions of a deity is an act driven by deliberate malice. "Mere printing or selling of textile materials containing artistic depictions of a deity or revered icon, even if appearing on portions of a garment near the lower border or Pallu, cannot automatically be presumed to be an act driven by deliberate malice or calculated to disrupt public order," the Court said. items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has initiated suo motu contempt of court proceedings against the editors-in-chief and publishers of The Hindu and Dainik Bhaskar for publishing Dera Sacha Sauda advertisements claiming that its chief, Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh, was being targeted as part of a conspiracy. The matter was today listed before a bench of Justice Vinod S Bhardwaj and Justice Ravinder Malik . The Court listed it for consideration on November 25. Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh is currently serving a 20-year sentence for raping his two disciples. His appeal challenging the conviction and sentence is pending before the High Court. The High Court in 2024 and in March this year had acquitted him in two different murders cases. On September 12, the newspapers published a front-page advertisement which claimed that there was a conspiracy against Ram Rahim. The Hindu later issued a public apology for publishing the advertisement following public backlash. The issue has now got revived in view of the suo motu contempt proceedings initiated on an order passed by Justice Subhas Mehla who said the newspaper advertisements insinuated that courts were a party to the alleged conspiracy.
